raw_graphql_pull_request.body: # [metrics] Export radix cache size gauges (entry count + total tokens) ## Motivation There is no direct metric for "how much is currently in the cache" / "roughly how many requests can it hold". Operators can see pool-level `kv_*` numbers, but not the radix tree's own footprint (node count) or total cached tokens as a single value. This adds two footprint gauges, aligned with #15699. ## Modifications - `RadixCache.get_cache_stats() -> (entry_count, total_tokens)`: `total_tokens` from the incrementally-maintained `evictable_size_ + protected_size_` (O(1), exact device-resident tokens); `entry_count` from an O(n) traversal of non-evicted nodes. - Two gauges on `RadixCacheMetricsCollector` (`multiprocess_mode="mostrecent"`): `sglang:cache_entry_count`, `sglang:cache_total_tokens`, plus `set_cache_size()`. - The scheduler pushes them from the **throttled** metrics path (`SchedulerMetricsMixin._log_radix_cache_size`, called next to `_log_hicache_stats()` in both the prefill and decode stats reporters), guarded by `hasattr` + `try/except` so footprint reporting can never break the scheduler loop. The O(n) traversal only runs at the metrics-log cadence, never on the request hot path. Files: - `python/sglang/srt/mem_cache/radix_cache.py` - `python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py` - `python/sglang/srt/observability/scheduler_metrics_mixin.py` ## Coverage / limitations `get_cache_stats()` lives on `RadixCache` (inherited by `HiRadixCache` / `LMCRadixCache`). Other tree caches without the method are a graceful no-op (the `hasattr` guard) and left as follow-up. ## Test process (verified on a live deployment) - Engine: `sglang` v0.5.12 (cu129), model **MiniMax-M2.7**, `tp=8/ep=8` on 8×GPU, `--enable-metrics --enable-hierarchical-cache`. - Relaunched with `--max-total-tokens 40000` so the footprint numbers are easy to sanity-check against the pool size. - Sent a batch of `/generate` requests to populate the radix tree, waited one metrics-push interval, then `curl localhost:30000/metrics`. - Before the patch, `cache_entry_count` / `cache_total_tokens` did not exist in `/metrics`. ## Key logs / sample output (real, captured) ``` sglang:cache_entry_count{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 69 sglang:cache_total_tokens{cache_type="HiRadixCache"} 38757 ``` `cache_total_tokens` (38757) tracks the ~40000-token KV pool as it fills, and `cache_entry_count` (69 nodes) lets you derive average prefix length / fragmentation (`38757 / 69 ≈ 562 tokens/node`). Together with `rate(sglang:evicted_tokens_total[5m])` this gives the effective cache horizon (capacity ÷ churn). ## Checklist - [x] Start a server with `--enable-metrics`, attach a `curl /metrics` sample (above). - [x] Verified the gauges update across the throttled metrics cadence as the cache fills. - [ ] Add a unit test for `get_cache_stats()`. > related: #15699 --- ## PR series / dependencies This is one of four independent observability PRs (a "cache observability" series). **None of them depend on each other to build or merge**, and they can be merged in any order: - `[router] cache-aware decision observability` (gateway / Rust) - `[metrics] cache eviction lifetime/frequency (L1+L2)` (engine / Python) - `[metrics] radix cache size gauges` (engine / Python) - `[tracing] per-request cache-match snapshot` (engine / Python) Notes: - The two `[metrics]` engine PRs touch `metrics_collector.py` and `radix_cache.py` in **different regions**; whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase. - The `[tracing]` per-request `cache_match` event is designed to **correlate** with the gateway routing span (the `[router]` PR) via the W3C `trace_id`, but it is fully functional on its own. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #29177965801](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29177965801) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #29177965718](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/29177965718)

nodes.body:
Cache-observability series (independent, any merge order):
- #28509 `[router]` cache-aware decision observability (gateway/Rust)
- #28507 `[metrics]` cache eviction lifetime/frequency L1+L2 (engine)
- #28508 `[metrics]` radix cache size gauges (engine)
- #28510 `[tracing]` per-request cache-match snapshot (engine)

Only coupling: #28507 and #28508 edit `metrics_collector.py`/`radix_cache.py` in different spots (trivial rebase if stacked); #28510's `cache_match` event correlates with #28509's routing span via `trace_id` but works standalone.
Pushed an update: `get_cache_stats()` failures now `logger.warning(...)` (instead of being silently swallowed) while still never breaking the scheduler loop.

I re-tested this on top of the latest `main` and everything works as expected. Setup: an SGLang deployment serving an FP8 model with hierarchical cache enabled (L1 GPU + L2 host) behind the cache-aware router (2 workers). I merged #28507, #28508, #28510 (engine) together with #28509 (router) onto the current `main`, rebuilt the images, and drove mixed traffic — repeated shared-prefix prompts to force cache hits plus a large number of distinct long prompts to force L1/L2 eviction — then scraped the metrics through Prometheus/Grafana. All the new metrics are emitted and populated with sane values: - Engine (`sglang:` prefix): cache_entry_count, cache_total_tokens, evicted_tokens_total, cache_eviction_events_total, cache_eviction_age_seconds (histogram), cache_eviction_reuses (histogram), hicache_host_evicted_tokens_total, hicache_host_eviction_age_seconds (histogram). - Router cache-aware decision metrics: the policy-branch counter(cache_hit / cache_miss_min_load / ...), the match-rate summary, and the per-worker tree-size gauge. Everything flowed into Prometheus and rendered correctly across all the corresponding Grafana panels (eviction lifetime/frequency, radix cache footprint/capacity, and gateway cache-aware decisions). No issues observed.

Thanks @chenkaiyue. Closing this because it has had no updates in 91 days.

Reopen it if the work is still relevant.

Some directories moved recently, so an older branch may need retargeting:
`sgl-kernel/` -> `python/sglang/kernels/aot/`, `python/sglang/jit_kernel/`
-> `python/sglang/kernels/jit/`, `docs/` -> `docs/docs/` (`.mdx`),
`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces radix cache capacity and footprint observability by exposing metrics for the radix cache entry count and total tokens. These metrics are tracked via Prometheus gauges and updated periodically during prefill and decode stats reporting. The review feedback suggests logging a warning instead of silently ignoring exceptions when retrieving cache stats, ensuring that any failures in metrics collection can be diagnosed without disrupting the scheduler loop.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> The [consumer version of Gemini Code Assist on GitHub](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/review-repo-code) is being sunset. Starting **June 18, 2026**, new organization installations will be blocked, and all code review activity will officially cease on **July 17, 2026**.
> For more details on the timeline and next steps, please review the [Help Documentation](https://developers.google.com/gemini-code-assist/docs/deprecations/consumer-code-review).

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

When an exception occurs during `get_cache_stats()`, it is silently ignored. While it is important that footprint reporting never breaks the scheduler loop, logging the exception at a `warning` level can help operators diagnose issues with metrics collection if they arise.

```suggestion
        try:
            entry_count, total_tokens = tree_cache.get_cache_stats()
        except Exception as e:
            # Footprint reporting must never break the scheduler loop.
            logger.warning(f"Failed to get radix cache stats: {e}")
            return
```

Since report_prefill_stat/report_decode_stat is a high-frequency operation, traversing the radix tree every time feels like a significant performance overhead. Could we consider maintaining the entry count directly within the radix tree?

OK, you're right. The decode path is gated by decode_log_interval, but the prefill path calls this on every prefill batch, so the O(n) walk can add up on a large tree. Fixed in the latest commit:

entry_count_ is now maintained incrementally at the node create/delete sites (_split_node / _insert_helper / _delete_leaf in RadixCache, plus the HiRadixCache overrides _insert_helper / _insert_helper_host / _split_node / evict_host, and the extra insert path in LMCRadixCache). get_cache_stats() is now O(1) and no longer traverses the tree.

One deliberate semantics note: the old traversal skipped evicted nodes. For RadixCache this is identical; for HiRadixCache the incremental counter now reports the total number of tree nodes (including host-only/device-evicted nodes still resident in the tree), which I think matches the cache_entry_count intent better. The docstring reflects this.

Verified on a real serving image (sglang, tp deployment): a randomized reconciliation of the incremental counter against a fresh O(n) traversal matched at every step across 4000 ops × page_size 1/4/8, and the counter drains back to 0 after full eviction.
